title: Karol G turns State Farm Stadium into a dazzling celebration - azcentral.com and The Arizona Republic
content: The party started long before the first note was played. By 5 p.m., waves of orange, pink and sparkling sequins had taken over the area surrounding State Farm Stadium, where cowboy boots, wide-brimmed hats and Latin American flags signaled that Karol G’s night was already underway. With hours still to go before the Colombian superstar took the stage, fans were already in full celebration mode. The photo booths set up inside the stadium quickly became one of the night's biggest attractions. Some fans waited in line for more than an hour to capture a souvenir photo, while others showed off outfits carefully planned for the occasion: tropical dresses and shirts, pink and orange ensembles, cowboy hats, boots and, of course, plenty of sequins. Karol G took the stage to the beat of "Latina Foreva” and “Un Gatito Me Llamó.” It took only minutes for her to trigger one of the evening’s loudest cheers when she tweaked a lyric to sing, “Sorry, no puedo porque hoy estoy en Phoenix” ("Sorry, I can’t, because today I’m in Phoenix"). The Colombian star followed with a blend of “OKI DOKI” and “Tá OK” before addressing her fans for the first time. “Hey, Phoenix! Wow! Look at the energy in this packed place. We came here to have una 'chimba' (an amazing time), right? I don’t know about you, but we came here to dance, cry, sing and celebrate,” she said. For the next two hours, much of the crowd remained on its feet, singing along, dancing and following every move of the Colombian performer as she turned the stadium into one massive party. “QLONA” kept the 'perreo' going before Karol G paused to acknowledge something that had clearly caught her attention: her fans’ outfits. “Seriously, the outfits are incredible. The way you all prepare for these shows amazes me every time,” she told the crowd. “I’m always blown away by all the sparkles, the orange outfits, some of you dressed in blue. Let’s sing this one together.” Afterward, Karol G disappeared from the stage, giving the massive screens center stage as they set up one of the night’s most theatrical and colorful segments. Actor Edward James Olmos appeared on screen with a message delivered in Spanglish, celebrating Latino pride and culture while introducing the next chapter of the show: Tropicoqueta. The Colombian returned completely transformed. She emerged wearing an oversized red-and-orange feathered headdress, a matching top and skirt, and red boots accented with yellow details. Her dancers completed the vibrant scene in colorful costumes and feather fans. Then, a giant scarlet macaw rose from the center of the stage, its wings stretching out in shades of yellow, blue and green. Karol G climbed aboard the towering bird to perform “Papasito,” turning the stadium into a dazzling spectacle of color and movement. The musical journey through Latin America was just beginning. “Amiga Mía” brought a touch of bachata to the set before Mariachi Reyna de Los Ángeles took the stage to perform the iconic “El Son de la Negra” while Karol G slipped away for another costume change. She returned for “Ese Hombre Es Malo,” now wearing a glittering red bolero jacket and matching bow, leaning fully into the Mexican-inspired segment of the show. “Mexico, thank you,” she told the crowd. “I owe so much to your culture, which has connected with me since I was a little girl. Tonight, I want us to celebrate this beautiful tradition.” Karol G then sang part of the song a cappella, letting the audience carry the melody before launching into “MAMIII.” Following another quick exit, she reappeared in blue sequin pants and a white shirt with matching blue sleeves emblazoned with the phrase “Single But Not Available,” a nod to “Te Llevas To” from her latest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. “Let’s see if Phoenix knows this one,” she challenged. Moments later, “Ahí,” her collaboration with Drake, filled the stadium. The crowd answered by singing every word and dancing along. “Hey, Phoenix, if you know this one, sing it as loud as you can so everyone can hear you,” she said before launching into the cumbia track “Alguien Que Te Amaba,” this time sporting a black cowboy hat. “We’re all together here, having an incredible night,” she added later. The celebration continued with “Si Lo Ven,” “El Barco” and “Verano Rosa.” One of the night’s most memorable moments came when Karol G decided the stage would no longer be hers alone. The Colombian superstar invited several fans onstage during “BbY WOW,” turning them into part of the show’s choreography. Fans from Mexico, El Salvador, and Panama sang, danced, and celebrated alongside her as giant screens lit up with a message that read: “PHOENIX, ustedes son Bby WOW.” The crowd responded with thunderous cheers, embracing a moment that felt less like a performance and more like a shared celebration. After another brief exit, Karol G returned in a sparkling gold sequin top and matching shorts, perched atop three oversized golden conga drums as she performed “Ivonny Bonita.” The high-energy segment continued with “Pineapple,” followed by a hit-filled medley featuring “A Su Boca La Amo,” “GATÚBELA” and “Rompe La Dompe.” By then, the party atmosphere inside State Farm Stadium had reached full force, with thousands of fans singing, dancing and matching Karol G’s energy song after song. For a few minutes, the distance between superstar and audience disappeared. As she performed “AMARGURA,” Karol G made her way along the runway, stopping to interact with fans, pose for photos and soak in the energy of the crowd. The intimate connection continued during “Tu Perfume,” giving fans some of the closest moments of the night. The main stage screens began displaying images of waterfalls as the action shifted to the secondary stage, transformed into a massive blue-lit rock formation surrounded by water. Shortly afterward, her dancers entered carrying silver water jugs and began splashing her as they danced to the rhythm of “Bandida Entrenada” and “OJOS FERRARI.” Throughout the night, the concert was as much a feast for the eyes as it was for the ears. Fireworks, towering flames, dazzling light displays and cascading water effects accompanied different songs, while the massive stage transformed from one act to the next. The main set, built around a towering rocky wall and a pyramid-like structure at its center, constantly evolved through projections, colors and special effects. The concert became a feast for the senses throughout the night. Fireworks, bursts of flame, light displays and water effects accompanied different songs, while the massive screens and the main stage, built around a towering rocky wall with a pyramid-like staircase at its center, transformed with each segment of the show. At times there was fire; at others, waterfalls, messages, vibrant colors on the screens and dancers splashing water on Karol G. Together, it all became part of a massive production designed to keep the audience engaged for more than two hours. Another message from Edward James Olmos signaled the beginning of the show's final chapter. “Even when we go far away, the heart longs for home. Sometimes the little things are what bring us back. A song, a flavor, a photograph. And suddenly, you’re home again,” the actor said. “And if the morning star (Lucero) has reminded us of anything tonight, it’s that you can travel all over the world, but your roots always travel right here, in your heart,” he continued. The message was then followed by an invitation for fans to raise their flags and celebrate where they come from, the sounds they grew up with and the traditions that helped shape their identities. “Let’s celebrate and let Latin America be heard,” Olmos concluded. Karol G emerged to the sound of “El Pescador,” accompanied by her dancers and dressed entirely in red: a one-sleeve top, low-rise wide-leg pants with a long train and a red headscarf. Then came one of the most emotional moments of the night. “It’s time to take out your flags and let them fly, fly, fly with pride, Phoenix,” the Colombian singer told the crowd. From the stage, she began identifying the countries represented throughout the stadium. “I see flags tonight from El Salvador, Puerto Rico, Panama, Honduras, Guatemala, Peru, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Mexico and, of course, from my home: Colombia!” Flags soon began waving throughout the stands, turning State Farm Stadium into a giant mosaic of Latin America. Karol G then removed the long train from her outfit and launched into “Tusa,” another of the night’s loudest singalongs. She still found time to organize a cheering contest between the left and right sides of the stadium, making sure not to forget fans seated in the upper levels. Then came “Coleccionando Heridas,” which was once again sung back word for word by the crowd. But one of the most anticipated moments of the night was still to come. “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido” turned State Farm Stadium into one giant chorus as thousands of fans sang and danced along to one of Karol G’s biggest hits, taking the tropical celebration in Glendale to another level. After more than two hours of music, choreography, costume changes and a journey through the sounds of Latin America, it was finally time to say goodbye. At 10:37 p.m., Karol G closed the night with “Provenza.” The same artist who had promised at the beginning of the show that Phoenix would dance, cry, sing and celebrate was now bringing the journey to an end. Karol G thanked her fans one last time before slowly descending beneath the center of the stage. When the lights came on, another thing became clear: Karol G’s appeal spans generations. Among the thousands in attendance were young girls, teenagers and adults. Entire families made their way out of the stands still wearing cowboy hats, boots, sequins, tropical outfits and flags draped over their shoulders. Most fans interviewed after the show agreed they had witnessed a memorable performance and left the stadium satisfied. Some, however, had been hoping for one more surprise: a special guest, as had happened at other stops on the tour. In Glendale, that moment never came. But it also never felt necessary. “I loved it! The colors, the vibe and the energy were excellent. The only thing missing was a special guest, since other cities got one,” said Goodyear resident Zoila Rodriguez. Rather than bringing out a surprise performer, Karol G put the spotlight on her own fans, inviting them onto the stage, interacting with them throughout the night and turning the stands into a mosaic of Latin American flags. Outside, shortly after 11 p.m., the sequins, hats and flags began to disperse across Glendale. And among those leaving the stadium lingered the feeling that they had just experienced a massive Latin celebration. content: The estimated 2027 GS base pay table is based on President Trump's alternative pay plan for federal employees. President Trump’s 2027 alternative pay plan letter issued on August 26, 2026, recommended freezing the General Schedule (GS) pay scale for 2027, leaving base pay and locality pay unchanged from 2026 rates for most federal civilian employees. However, the letter also authorizes a separate 3.8% pay increase for federal law enforcement personnel. The letter follows through on the White House’s 2027 budget proposal, which did not include a civilian pay raise. Congress has not passed legislation setting a different 2027 pay adjustment, and the freeze won’t be official until Trump signs an executive order in December which is the step that actually locks in next year’s pay tables. No new locality pay areas or boundary changes are expected for 2027. The Federal Salary Council had recommended new standalone localities for the Kennewick-Richland-Walla Walla, Washington, and Syracuse-Auburn, New York, areas, along with boundary expansions in Ohio and Arizona. The President’s Pay Agent rejected those recommendations in its December 2025 annual report, stating it would not approve further additions to existing locality pay areas or the creation of new ones “at this time.” Yes. title: Karol G’s ‘BbY WOW’ Lyrics & English Translation: What Song Does It Sample? - Just Jared
content: The 35-year-old Colombian superstar’s “BbY WOW” with Judeline and Rusowsky, featured on her new album NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO, is steadily surging up the streaming charts, and fans are eagerly looking up the lyrics and English translation, as well as the familiar song it samples. As of the end of August, the song broke through the Billboard Hot 100 to No. 38, and is already a No. 1 hit on US Hot Latin Songs and Hot Latin Rhythm Songs charts. Karol broke down the story behind the song in an in-depth interview for Rolling Stone. I felt like I needed a song, one that people could dance to in the club but that also had that emotion. So, what happens when you’re in the club and you’re heartbroken? You just think about the other person, about the song you’d love to be dancing to with that person. The first version of the song was just me. But I felt like, live, I wanted to sing that song with more people on stage and for it to really become a bit more of a party. And that’s when I thought of Rusowsky and I said to Judeline, “Why don’t you join the song?” I worked a lot on that album with Judeline because the way she sings about love made me feel how men sometimes don’t understand how deep a woman’s pain can be. She has something special, and it’s that every emotion feels so intense. She has a song called “Is God Good or Just Powerful?” It’s literally one that lasts about a minute and a half. What she sings is super short, it’s like a verse and a chorus. And I was like, “Wow, how can you say so much in a verse and a chorus?” So it was literally a must for me to write music with her for this album. Our teams got in touch. We told her I was making new music and she traveled to Los Angeles. I spent about a week with her, and it was really nice because the first thing we did was sit down and talk, like, “I’ll give you some context about where I am, how I’m feeling.”We were both going through almost the same thing, so I loved that because we were in sync and it just worked. I thought, “We’re both here, feeling almost the same thing, it’s going to flow in a special way.”We were in the studio for about three or four days, and we made more music there that isn’t on the album. The song samples the “Coolie Dance” riddim by Cordell ‘Scatta’ Burrell and Everton, as popularized on “Move Ya Body,” the 2004 hit by Nina Sky featuring Jabba and Kat DeLuna‘s “Whine Up,” among other hits over the years. Kehlani also used it on 2024’s “After Hours.” Posted To:Cordell Burrell Jabba Judeline Karol G Music Nina Sky No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto Rusowsky

title: Vikings Mourn Death of Former QB & Punter Bob Lee - vikings.com
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings are mourning the loss of former quarterback and punter Bob Lee, who passed away Aug. 17, just 10 days after he turned 81. Lee holds the distinction of punting in Minnesota's first Super Bowl appearance (IV) and throwing the most recent touchdown by a Viking in a Super Bowl (XI), a 13-yarder caught by Stu Voigt in the fourth quarter against the Raiders. He made the Vikings roster in 1969 and played in the NFL through 1980, totaling 77 regular-season games played for Minnesota, Atlanta and the Los Angeles Rams. In 30 starts at quarterback, Lee posted a 19-11 record with the Vikings. He played in eight postseason games, making three starts. That's pretty impressive, considering he entered the NFL as a 17th-round pick (441st overall out of 462 picks) out of the University of the Pacific in 1968. Lee made his pro debut in the 1969 season opener, punting six times in a game at the Giants in which Fran Tarkenton led New York to a comeback win against his previous and future team. The following week, after Joe Kapp tied an NFL record with seven touchdown passes against the Baltimore Colts, Lee attempted his first pro passes, going 4-for-6 with 35 yards in the 52-14 Vikings win. Lee first met Kapp (with Vikings 1967-69) long before they became teammates. In fall 2019 both were among attendees during a 50th anniversary celebration of the 1969 NFL Champions. The reunion included panel discussions, during which Lee shared his memory of meeting Kapp the first time when Kapp was QB at Cal and Lee was 12. "I met Joe Kapp when I was 12 years old and he was a junior at the University of California on a 1-9 team," Lee explained. "My dad ran The Associated Press in San Francisco. They were in competition with other wire services. They hired a college senior journalism student to do the postgame stories. Those stories for the Eastern papers paid a nickel a word. They were 1,500 words, so 75 bucks, which was a big deal in 1957. "The senior didn't show up. They said, 'The press pass works. Go down there, write a bunch of notes. We'll turn it into a story.' The first guy I listened to was Joe Kapp," Lee continued. "Joe took all the blame for the loss. Nobody else. It was his fault. … He was a leader. He didn't push himself in certain directions on other people." Lee attempted one pass in a 51-3 win over Cleveland on Nov. 9, 1969, and went 3-for-4 with his first touchdown, a 7-yard strike to John Henderson in a 52-14 win over the Steelers two weeks later. During the 1969 postseason, Lee punted three times in a 23-20 win over the Rams and thrice more in a 27-7 victory over the Browns, helping Minnesota advance to Super Bowl IV. He punted three times in that game as well. After making two starts as a backup late in 1970 but not punting that season, he returned to those duties in 1971. Lee made four starts in the regular season, as well as the playoff game against Dallas in the Divisional Round. Lee also handled punting duties in that loss to the Cowboys. That was the final time he punted in an NFL game. Tarkenton's return to Minnesota in 1972 led to Lee returning to a reserve QB role before he was traded to Atlanta in 1973, when he posted his best results, going 8-2 for the Falcons. After one more season there, he returned to Minnesota in 1975. Lee backed up Tarkenton over the next four seasons and went 4-1 in five starts from 1976-77. "Bob Lee was under appreciated at how good he was at quarterback," Tarkenton said. "He was a great backup QB for us and a good starter for the Atlanta Falcons. Plus, Bob was an absolutely great human being that you could depend on anytime. He was as good of a teammate as you could ever have." When Tarkenton suffered a broken leg in mid-November of the 1977 season, Lee won three of four starts to help Minnesota finish 9-5. Playing through a broken right hand during the stretch, he then quarterbacked the Vikings to a win over the Rams in the Divisional Round of the NFC Playoffs, a game that came to be known as the "Mud Bowl." "Playing on a field like this is worse than snow," Lee said after the game. "You're slipping, your runners are slipping and your receivers are slipping. I think the thing that I was most impressed by was the way our ball carriers and receivers held onto the ball. It's kind of amazing that we didn't have one turnover." Rams QB Pat Haden threw interceptions to Nate Allen, Paul Krause and Jeff Wright. The Cowboys, however, prevailed over the Vikings in the NFC Championship Game on the way to a convincing win in Super Bowl XII. Lee capped his career with two seasons as a backup with the Rams. His final scoring pass was a 41-yarder against the Vikings in a pivotal 27-21 overtime win for L.A. From 1991-96 Lee proudly served as director of athletics at University of the Pacific, helping expand the school's athletics and fitness facilities. He became one of 22 charter members in the Pacific Athletics Hall of Fame in 1982. Other roles Lee held including serving on the board of directors for the Northern California chapter of the National Football Foundation and Hall of Fame, as well as chairman of the San Francisco Special Olympics in 1981. © 2026 Minnesota Vikings Football, LLC , All Rights Reserved. title: BMW R 1300 GS: The Adventure Bike That Eliminates The Need For A Second Motorcycle - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Owning multiple motorcycles sounds like the dream. You have one for weekday commuting, another for weekend canyon roads, and a third to disappear into the wilderness. Reality, however, slaps you in the face and reminds you that more motorcycles mean higher insurance costs, more maintenance, and more garage space. That's why many riders don't look for a bike that satisfies just one purpose, but one that handles a wide variety of rides. Motorcycles capable of handling nearly every situation have become more desirable over the years, and adventure bikes are leading that charge. A one-bike garage is simple. You don’t divide riding time between specialized machines. Instead, with every passing mile, you build familiarity with a single motorcycle. You learn its strengths, understand its personality, and develop your confidence in your skills, regardless of whether the road ahead looks freshly paved or covered in loose gravel. Adventure motorcycles have become the biggest reason why single-bike ownership is a realistic option. They combine upright ergonomics, long-travel suspension, generous luggage options, and capable engines, allowing riders to travel wherever they choose, be it their workplace or a remote village few others have visited. ADVs have steadily evolved into some of the most versatile machines on the market. While early generations leaned heavily toward either off-road exploration or long-distance touring, today’s flagship bikes are engineered to do both exceptionally well. They get large fuel capacities, advanced electronics, adaptive suspension, sophisticated rider aids, and increasingly refined engines. Riders today don't even have to choose between highway comfort and off-road capability, because most modern ADVs are designed to deliver both in the same package. Now, if you are looking for something that balances everything perfectly, there is exactly one bike for it. Need to commute? The bike feels manageable despite its size. Planning a thousand-mile road trip? This is built for exactly that. Curious about what’s at the end of a dirt track? Long-travel suspension and enduro equipment to the rescue. For decades, the BMW GS family has become the benchmark against which nearly every large ADV is measured. The R 1300 GS continues that legacy while introducing one of the most comprehensive redesigns the model has ever received. Compared with the previous R 1250 GS, almost every major component has been reworked. There is a new steel sheet-metal main frame, a die-cast aluminum rear frame, a more compact boxer engine, lower overall weight, updated suspension, and significantly expanded electronic capabilities. BMW also focused heavily on improving everyday usability. The lower center of gravity thanks to the boxer engine contributes to low-speed balance, while an optional automated transmission and adaptive ride height reduce intimidation for shorter riders. The result is an adventure bike that appeals equally to world travelers and daily commuters alike. At the heart of the BMW R 1300 GS sits a 1,300 cc air/liquid-cooled flat twin engine (best known as a boxer twin) that churns out 145 horsepower at 7,750 rpm and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 rpm. This makes it one of the most powerful production boxer engines BMW has ever installed in one of its motorcycles. The best part? Despite the increased output and capacity, the engine is actually more compact than before. BMW repositioned the transmission beneath the engine while redesigning the overall layout to save space and reduce weight. Now, the engine’s personality changes dramatically depending on how the motorcycle is configured. Power delivery is broad, but the ride modes allow the rider to adjust throttle response and traction to their particular use case. There is an ECO mode that incorporates BMW's ShiftCam technology. This varies valve timing and valve lift to improve fuel economy as well as power delivery on long stretches of highway. The R 1300 GS also comes with a six-speed gearbox as standard. However, optionally, you can ask for the Automated Shift Assistant. This allows for fully automatic shifting or manual operation without a conventional clutch lever. A welcome feature when you consider what a burden stop-and-go traffic can be on the daily commute. The R 1300 GS represents one of the most comprehensive redesigns in the model's history. BMW replaced the tubular steel frame with an entirely new steel sheet-metal main frame for increased rigidity and tighter packaging size. The rear, too, has a new die-cast aluminum lattice rear frame. This is suspended on BMW's signature EVO Telelever front suspension and EVO Paralever rear suspension, while braking is handled by two 310 mm discs at the front with four-piston radial calipers, and a single 285 mm disc at the rear clamped by a two-piston floating caliper. Now, suspension technology has become one of the biggest advantages of premium adventure motorcycles, and the R 1300 GS pushes that even further. BMW’s Dynamic Suspension Adjustment continuously adapts damping characteristics according to riding conditions, throttle inputs, speed, and road surface. This is optional, but combined with the adaptive vehicle height features, it makes low-speed maneuvers, starts and stops, and parking considerably easier, even with a full load of luggage strapped to the bike. Although completely redesigned, the BMW R 1300 GS remains instantly recognizable as a GS. The signature boxer engine continues to define its silhouette, and the bodywork is noticeably more compact, improving both balance and reach to the ground. Ergonomics place the rider in a commanding upright position, giving them excellent control and reduced fatigue during long journeys. You also get multiple seat heights, adjustable ergonomics, luggage systems, and comfort packages to tailor the bike for touring, off-road expeditions, or even everyday riding. The R 1300 GS showcases just how sophisticated adventure motorcycles have become. A full-color TFT display provides navigation, smartphone connectivity, riding data, and vehicle information. LED lighting comes standard, while an optional adaptive headlight actively follows the motorcycle through corners. Radar-based Riding Assistant tech introduces active cruise control, front collision warning, lane change warning, and rear-end collision warning. Keyless ride, heated grips, tire pressure monitoring, hill start control, engine drag torque control, and numerous other electronic rider aids round out an already extensive suite of technology.​​​​​​​ Replacing multiple motorcycles is an ambitious goal, but the BMW R 1300 GS comes remarkably close. It possesses enough comfort for long-distance touring, enough performance to satisfy spirited road riding, enough capability for genuine off-road exploration, and enough practicality to function as everyday transportation. The search for the perfect all-around motorcycle has always been difficult, but the GS blends those qualities more effectively than most of its rivals. We want to hear from you. title: Vikings at Broncos Game Observations - vikings.com
content: DENVER — The Vikings preseason wrapped Friday night with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback and playing two series before handing the reins of Minnesota's offense to Max Brosmer. Minnesota Head Coach Kevin O'Connell and Denver Head Coach Sean Payton opted to rest starters on both sides of the ball in the 34-6 Broncos win. O'Connell had hoped J.J. McCarthy was able to recover from an ankle injury suffered on a hit the previous week against the Baltimore Ravens. McCarthy was limited in practice early in the week and did not participate at all Wednesday in a practice that had more of a scrimmage format. Wentz finished 3-for-4 passing with 15 yards and a passer rating of 80.2. His longest completion was a gain of 6 to tight end Gavin Bartholomew. Brosmer opened by hitting his first few short completions and drove the Vikings 55-yards into the red zone late in the second quarter before the drive stalled in the red zone. Will Reichard booted a 28-yard field goal to cap the drive that lasted 4:00. The only problem was Denver stormed right back by driving 65 yards in just 1:08 thanks to Sam Ehlinger going 4-for-5 and accounting for all 65 yards through the air. Jaleel McLaughlin capped the drive with a 20-yard catch-and-run touchdown, securing the grab on the right side and showing his speed as he zoomed to the left. Brosmer finished 20-of-35 passing with 166 yards and a passer rating of 69.5 Ehlinger finished 15-for-20 with 233 yards and three scores. His passer rating was 131.9. View game action photos from the Vikings preseason game vs. the Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas had really been making the most of his opportunities and started on Friday along with third-round pick Jakobe Thomas, who made his pro debut after missing Minnesota's first two preseason contests because of back tightness. Jacob Thomas unfortunately suffered an injury while defending a pass on the seventh play of the game. He was slow to get up after landing out of bounds. It was a tough end to a preseason that had started with such promise for Thomas, who recorded an interception at New York in his NFL debut. Jacob Thomas was replaced by Kahlef Hailassie, who recorded an interception in the second quarter to set up Minnesota's first score. Linebacker Jacob Roberts, who had recorded Minnesota's other interception against the Giants, also left the game with an injury. One of the battles that hadn't yielded much indication is at punter where veteran Johnny Hekker and undrafted rookie Brett Thorson. It likely wasn't going to be decided by Friday's action alone, which is good because the stats were about as even as possible. Thorson punted three times for 156 yards for an average of 52.0 and with a long of 58. Hekker? Three punts for 156 yards and an average of 52.0 with a long of 57. Times inside the 20-yard line? Twice each for both players. Ehlinger enjoyed a fourth quarter for the ages. He was able to orchestrate a 17-play 85 yard drive that lasted 9:58 and concluded with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Cody Schrader on fourth-and-2 with 13:04 remaining. Ehlinger also capitalized on a busted coverage that left rookie tight end Justin Joly completely uncovered in the middle of the field. Joly was able to catch it and run for an 88-yard score to cap a 93-yard drive that lasted just three plays and 1:39. Minnesota was unable to push the ball down the field much and finished with 270 yards. The Vikings went 3-for-13 on third downs and averaged 4.7 yards per play. The Vikings concluded the season with just one touchdown across three games (a fade from Wentz to Myles Price at New York). Minnesota went 0-for-2 on trips inside Denver's 20-yard line.
